# Founding Account Executive — Industrial AI (Series A)

 Posted Aug 20, 2026 

Founding US-based Account Executive

Snapshot: $120K–$150K base · $240K–$300K OTE + equity · Remote (US East Coast) · Up to 50% travel · No visa sponsorship · 3–7 yrs enterprise SaaS

THE OPPORTUNITY

Our client is a fast-growing, Series A AI company (~50 people, European HQ) whose video-based AI agents monitor, optimize, and automate industrial production. Growth is standout: ARR up 5x in the past year and net revenue retention above 380%. As the first US commercial hire, you'll build the North American GTM from scratch, working directly with the CEO on six- and seven-figure deals into manufacturing and industrial accounts.

### WHAT YOU'LL DO

Build, own, and scale a pipeline across manufacturing and industrial verticals. Grow six-figure deals into seven-figure, multi-site AI programs through expansion. Navigate complex enterprise buying cycles with executive and operational stakeholders. Partner with the CEO and product/engineering to shape US GTM and roadmap. Travel up to 50% for on-site prospect and customer engagement.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

First 90 days: learn the product and industrial buyer, build a US pipeline, and advance early deals. First year: land and expand the first multi-site programs and establish the repeatable US motion.

MUST-HAVES

3–7 years enterprise SaaS/software sales with consistent quota attainment; experience selling into industrial, manufacturing, IIoT, or automation environments; self-starter comfortable in early-stage, high-ownership settings; valid driver's license and willingness to travel up to 50%.

NICE-TO-HAVES

Experience as a first/founding sales hire; computer-vision or video-analytics background; multi-site enterprise expansion experience.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

$120K–$150K base (USD), $240K–$300K OTE, competitive equity.

### LOCATION & WORK MODEL

Remote with an East Coast base; up to 50% travel across the US.

### ABOUT THIS SEARCH

This is a confidential search managed by our recruiting team on behalf of our client. We've kept the company name off the posting — apply and we'll share full details and introduce you directly. We're an equal-opportunity partner and welcome applicants of all backgrounds; compensation reflects the role's posted range.

# Description

What we build

Last year, natural catastrophes caused over $140 billion in US losses.

ResiQuant exists to keep the built world insurable as catastrophe intensifies.

Two nearly identical buildings can have completely different fates in an earthquake, hurricane, or wildfire — and the expertise necessary to tell them apart isn't available when underwriters need it most. That's where ResiQuant comes in.

Think Harvey, but for property underwriting: our AI agents do what used to take underwriting teams days and weeks — read messy broker submissions, virtually inspect buildings, validate the structural data that drives the vast majority of catastrophe loss variation, and price risk against a carrier's own guidelines — in minutes.

Who we are

A team of scientists, ex-founders, AI and structural engineers, and product builders from Pear and YC companies. Backed by LDV Capital, Pear VC, Foothill Ventures, and strategics. We've designed buildings, contributed to national building codes, and built products people love.

Co-founders **Omar Issa** and **Francisco Galvis** are structural engineering PhDs out of **Stanford's Blume Earthquake Engineering Center** — the birthplace of modern catastrophe modeling.

- Omar is a second-generation structural engineer who deployed on post-disaster response at Ridgecrest and served on NIST and USGS code committees; previously Arup and KATERRA.

- Francisco is a third-generation engineer who survived the 1999 Armenia, Colombia earthquake, ran post-earthquake inspections in Turkey and after Hurricane Ian, and led San Francisco's non-ductile concrete ordinance work; previously Thornton Tomasetti.

Every logo we have was closed by the two founders — mapping workflows with chief underwriting officers, shadowing underwriters through renewals, partnering with shops from startup MGAs to publicly traded carriers.
